verses.text: When Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he was furious and began mocking the Jews.

In front of his associates and the army of Samaria, he said, "What are these weak Jews doing? Do they think they can fortify the city? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they finish in a day? Can they bring burned stones back to life out of those piles of rubble?"
Tobiah the Ammonite was beside him. He said, "Even a fox climbing on that stone wall would knock it down."
Hear us, our God, because they despise us. Turn their insults back on them. Let them be plundered in a land where they're taken captive.
Don't cover their guilt or erase their sin from before you, because they've insulted the builders.
We kept building until the entire wall was joined up to half its height. The people were determined to work.
When Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the people of Ashdod heard that the repairs to Jerusalem's walls were moving ahead and the gaps were closing, they became furious.
They plotted together to attack Jerusalem and throw us into confusion.
We prayed to our God and posted guards day and night because of the threat.
Meanwhile, the people of Judah said, "The workers who carry the loads are wearing out. There's so much rubble that we can't rebuild the wall."
Our enemies said, "They won't know or see a thing until we're among them. Then we'll kill them and stop the work."
The Jews who lived near them came to warn us again and again from all directions: "Wherever you turn, they'll attack us."
So I stationed people in family groups at the lowest, most exposed places behind the wall, with their swords, spears, and bows.

After looking things over, I stood up and told the nobles, officials, and everyone else, "Don't be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome. Fight for your brothers, your sons and daughters, your wives, and your homes."
When our enemies heard that we knew about their plan and that God had frustrated it, we all went back to the wall, each to our work.
From then on, half my servants worked and half held spears, shields, bows, and armor. The officials stood behind all the people of Judah.
The builders and the people carrying supplies took up their loads, working with one hand and holding a weapon with the other.
Each builder wore a sword at his side while he worked, and the trumpeter stayed with me.
I told the nobles, officials, and everyone else, "This is a large job spread over a wide area, and we're working far apart along the wall.
When you hear the trumpet, gather where it sounds. Our God will fight for us."
We kept working, with half the men holding spears from dawn until the stars came out.
I also told the people, "Have each man and his servant spend the night in Jerusalem, so they can guard us at night and work during the day."
None of us took off our clothes, whether my brothers, my servants, the guards with me, or I. We took our weapons even when we went for water.
